## What's new

- **The interface does everything now.** Sign in, enter your R2 keys, add a
  folder, change what one includes, restore, rename, recover a deleted file,
  turn automatic backups on and off and change how often — all without
  leaving the window. Nothing tells you to go and run a command any more.

- **Four modes.** `1 Folders`, `2 Schedule`, `3 Trash`, `4 Account`, on
  number keys or <kbd>tab</kbd>. Scheduling in particular now has somewhere
  to live: what is registered, when it next runs, whether it runs while you
  are signed out.

- **Adding a folder means browsing to it.** No typing a path from memory —
  walk the disk, pick the folder, then untick what you do not want in the
  tree, then name it. It backs up straight away.

- **Every command still works exactly as it did.** The scheduler still runs
  `r2b backup`, your scripts are unaffected, and every flag means what it
  meant. The interface is a second front door, not a replacement.

## Fixed

- **Leaving mid-backup abandoned it.** Starting another job while a backup
  was running could wedge the upload partway with no sign anything was wrong.
  A second job is now refused while one is in flight, and the transfer can no
  longer be blocked by a screen that has gone away.

- **Layout on small terminals.** The frame could render a row taller than the
  window, which clipped the keyboard help off the bottom, and on an
  80-column terminal `q quit` scrolled off the end — a full-screen program
  with no visible way out.
